summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Half Skirt Production Tutorial ## Introduction In this video, we will learn how to make a uniform skirt. This tutorial covers the steps involved in creating various types of skirts, including the uniform skirt, pumpkin skirt, and bodycon skirt. ## Initial Setup First, open the button skirt and delete the extra panels. Then, copy a belt panel using `Ctrl+C` and `Ctrl+V`, and place it in the 2D window. Next, we can make it a little longer. This length will be the group length we create later. ## Resetting 2D Arrangement Activate the panel and right-click to reset the 2D arrangement position, as its grid may be broken. Now, let’s open this panel. ## Adding Internal Lines Before we proceed, I want to show you how to make a uniform skirt. First, add two internal lines in the middle. Then, select one internal line and use the folding line tool. When the folding angle is set to 0 degrees, this line will protrude outward from the front of the panel. If the front and back are not visible, remember to switch to the texture surface to check them. Conversely, setting the folding angle to 360 degrees will cause the line to bend inward from the front of the panel. To make the panel fold more clearly, I will choose to print this panel. When a panel is printed, all the internal lines and their folding angles will be retained to the maximum extent, resulting in clearer folds. ## Adjusting Panel Width After folding, we will see that the panel has only one-third of its width. To ensure that the folded panel emerges correctly, we need to make a panel that is three times wider. After deleting the extra internal lines, we will start making the flat panel. Select this panel, copy, and paste it until there are three panels in total. Then, select the middle lines and merge them. Be sure to delete any excess points. ## Merging Internal Lines Next, we will merge the internal lines used for folding in the middle. First, select the two-sided lines, right-click, and select the internal line generated according to the curve. For the expansion number, select \(3 \times - 1\). If the expansion number is set to 2, it can be cut into three sides, so this value must be \(3 - 1\). I will set it to 20. After selecting the internal line created, right-click and select align, then add points to the panel line. Let’s see what happens if we skip this step. Later, when we use the folding function, it is identified as a group of three lines, necessitating interruption of this line. ## Applying Fold Angles Select the internal lines, right-click, and select align again to add points to the panel line. After selecting, this will automatically interrupt the line. If we experience stretching during merging, we can reset the 2D arrangement position in 3D space. Now, use the fold tool. Press the left button on the first internal line and double-click on the right side of the last internal line to start applying the fold angle. This tool automatically applies the fold angle. First, choose the type to follow the fold, which is the direction of the clothing group. Select 3 for the internal line number of each fold; the other options do not need to be changed. Click to confirm, and you will see the internal line colors change to red and green, indicating the applied fold angles. ## Simulation and Sewing Before proceeding to sew, simulate the panel line in the 3D window. This allows it to fold properly before sewing it to the belt. After folding, rotate it to the side of the virtual model and repeat the fold angle. Then, copy and paste a panel line. Note that it should be a direct copy and paste, not a symmetrical or mirror copy, as the direction of the line is crucial. Now, sew the waistband, clicking from the left side of the pleats. First, sew the waistband, then click the starting point, drag along the mouse, and click again at the end. Start the simulation and wait for the panel to simulate. If the fold is not very obvious after simulation, we can print the panel first. ## Completing the Skirt After simulation, use the sewing machine to sew the front and back. Upon final completion, remove the hardening. You should now see that the folding direction remains unchanged from the bottom view. ## Modifying the Waistband Now let's take a look at how to modify the waistband. Many models have a much wider waist than the waist itself. If we use the whole waist to make the skirt, the front may look flat, while the back, being fuller, may cause the fold to expand. To modify the waistband, we may need to start over, as stretching it directly can cause interlocking issues. We will delete several sewing lines and repeat the operation, stretching the waistband wider. ## Final Touches Now I have two pleats of seam, and the waist is folded into the middle. We can see that the strap of the waist is too high, which means if we do not stitch the waistband from here, it will not be comfortable. Let’s apply the same technique on the other side. This is how one side looks, and if you fold the sides of the waist, you will end up with a very thin waistband. Thank you. ## Adjusting Fabric Properties When our board is wider, from the back it does not exhibit an obvious problem of expansion. You can also adjust the board to an arched shape. To prevent the board from deforming, we can copy a fabric and increase the strength of the gold-plated sandpaper or use Fusible Rigid. We can also make it look closer to physical properties on top. First, select the physical properties of this skirt part and reduce the strength of the gold-plated sandpaper slightly for a better hammering feel. Additionally, reduce the bending strength a little for a softer appearance. Adjust the particle diameter to reduce the small black spots caused by network gaps. ## Addressing Simulation Problems If the length of the board is not right, the skirt may appear wrinkled at the bottom. To smooth these wrinkles, polish the surface and use the stabilizer to adjust thermal resistance. Regardless of how high the thermal resistance is, we will adjust it through the properties in the physical editor. The deformation rate controls how easily the fabric deforms under external forces. For instance, when set to 100, the fold of the ferrous line will be smoothed without changing shape. ## Conclusion In summary, while creating a uniform skirt, common problems can arise, such as folds that should not be folding in. To address issues related to unstable simulations, we can adjust with a fixed needle tool. Select the edge, find the approximate position in the 2D or 3D window, and add a fixed needle along the edge of the hole. When we start the simulation, the board will automatically fold. Afterward, we can delete this fixed needle and proceed with the simulation. By carefully following these steps, you can create a well-structured uniform skirt that meets your design needs. Thank you for watching! ```
